entities.name: in list of a port type
out list of a port type

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port IS the means of communication between test components and between test components and the test system interface.
requirements.original: Ports facilitate communication between test components and between test components and the test system interface.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS supporting message-based ports and procedure-based ports.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports message-based and procedure-based ports.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type SHALL be defined as being either message-based or procedure-based.
requirements.original: Each port shall be defined as being message-based or procedure-based.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence says 'each port' but the kind is fixed in the port type definition (see next sentence).

requirements.subject: ent:message-based-port
requirements.canonical: A message-based port type definition SHALL be identified by the keyword `message`.
requirements.original: Message-based ports shall be identified by the keyword message and procedure-based ports shall be identified by the keyword `procedure` within the associated port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:procedure-based-port
requirements.canonical: A procedure-based port type definition SHALL be identified by the keyword `procedure`.
requirements.original: Message-based ports shall be identified by the keyword message and procedure-based ports shall be identified by the keyword `procedure` within the associated port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port IS bidirectional.
requirements.original: Ports are bidirectional.

requirements.subject: ent:port-direction
requirements.canonical: The communication direction of a port type list IS specified by the keyword `in` (in direction), `out` (out direction) or `inout` (both directions).
requirements.original: The directions are specified by the keywords `in` (for the in direction), `out` (for the out direction) and inout (for both directions).

requirements.subject: ent:in-list
requirements.canonical: The operations `getcall`, `reply` and `raise` MAY be applied to a signature present in the in list of a procedure-based port.
requirements.original: Operations allowed on a procedure present in the incoming port list are ` `getcall`, `reply` and `raise`.

ambiguity.issue: Only part of the rule is stated: it is unclear whether these are the only operations allowed, and the wording 'procedure' is used for signature; the sentence also contains a stray backtick.
readings: The operations `getcall`, `reply` and `raise` MAY be applied to a signature present in the in list of a procedure-based port.
Only the operations `getcall`, `reply` and `raise` SHALL be applied to a signature present only in the in list of a procedure-based port.

requirements.subject: ent:out-list
requirements.canonical: The operations `call`, `getreply` and `catch` MAY be applied to a signature present in the out list of a procedure-based port.
requirements.original: Operations allowed on a procedure present in the outcoming port list are `call`, `getreply` and `catch`.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence uses 'procedure' for signature and 'outcoming port list' (a typo) for the out list.

requirements.subject: ent:port-direction
requirements.condition: the port is not a test system interface port
requirements.canonical: The communication direction of a port SHALL be seen from the point of view of the test component owning the port.
requirements.original: Directions shall be seen from the point of view of the test component owning the port with the exception of the test system interface, where directions shall be seen from the point of view of the test component port mapped to the test system interface port.

requirements.subject: ent:port-direction
requirements.condition: the port is a port of the test system interface
requirements.canonical: The communication direction of a test system interface port SHALL be seen from the point of view of the test component port mapped to the test system interface port.
requirements.original: Directions shall be seen from the point of view of the test component owning the port with the exception of the test system interface, where directions shall be seen from the point of view of the test component port mapped to the test system interface port.

requirements.subject: ent:in-list
requirements.canonical: The in list of a test system interface port IS containing the message types and signatures for which the mapped test component port allows the operations `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `reply` or `raise`.
requirements.original: The in list of the test system interface port contains message or procedure for which the mapped test component port allows the following operations: `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `reply` or `raise`.

ambiguity.issue: 'contains' may describe what the in list must contain (a requirement on the declaration) or a consequence of the direction rule; also 'message or procedure' should be message types or signatures.
readings: The in list of a test system interface port IS containing the message types and signatures for which the mapped test component port allows `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `reply` or `raise`.
The in list of a test system interface port SHALL contain every message type and signature for which a mapped test component port allows `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `reply` or `raise`.

requirements.subject: ent:out-list
requirements.canonical: The out list of a test system interface port IS containing the message types and signatures for which the mapped test component port allows the operations `send`, `call`, `getreply` or `catch`.
requirements.original: The out list of the test system interface port contains message or procedure for which the mapped test component port allow the following operations: `send`, `call`, `getreplay` or `catch`.

ambiguity.issue: 'contains' may describe a requirement on the declaration or a consequence; 'getreplay' is a typo for `getreply`; 'message or procedure' should be message types or signatures.
readings: The out list of a test system interface port IS containing the message types and signatures for which the mapped test component port allows `send`, `call`, `getreply` or `catch`.
The out list of a test system interface port SHALL contain every message type and signature for which a mapped test component port allows `send`, `call`, `getreply` or `catch`.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type definition SHALL have one or more lists indicating the allowed message types or signatures together with the allowed communication direction.
requirements.original: Each port type definition shall have one or more lists indicating the allowed collection of (message) types or procedure signatures together with the allowed communication direction.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type MAY have one `map param` declaration indicating the allowed additional parameters of the `map` operation.
requirements.original: For configuration purposes the port type may have one **map param** and **one unmap param** declaration indicating the allowed additional parameters for the respective operation.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type MAY have one `unmap param` declaration indicating the allowed additional parameters of the `unmap` operation.
requirements.original: For configuration purposes the port type may have one **map param** and **one unmap param** declaration indicating the allowed additional parameters for the respective operation.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter of a `map param` or `unmap param` declaration SHALL be a value parameter.
requirements.original: These formal parameters shall be value parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:in-list
requirements.condition: a signature is defined in the out direction of a procedure-based port
requirements.canonical: If a signature is defined in the out direction of a procedure-based port, the types of all its `inout` and `out` parameters, its return type and its exception types ARE automatically part of the in direction of that port.
requirements.original: Whenever a signature (see also clause 14) is defined in the out direction of a procedure-based port, the types of all its inout and out parameters, its return type and its exception types are automatically part of the in direction of this port.

requirements.subject: ent:out-list
requirements.condition: a signature is defined in the in direction of a procedure-based port
requirements.canonical: If a signature is defined in the in direction of a procedure-based port, the types of all its `inout` and `out` parameters, its return type and its exception types ARE automatically part of the out direction of that port.
requirements.original: Whenever a signature is defined in the in direction for a procedure-based port, the types of all its inout and out parameters, its return type and its exception types are automatically part of the out direction of this port.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port used for communication with the SUT CAN need to address specific entities within the SUT.
requirements.original: Ports used for the communication with the SUT may need to address specific entities within the SUT.

requirements.subject: ent:sut
requirements.canonical: The SUT CAN support several address schemes at different ports.
requirements.original: In addition, several address schemes may be supported by one SUT at different ports.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: An address type MAY be bound to a port type.
requirements.original: To support such addressing schemes, TTCN-3 allows to bind an address type to a port.

ambiguity.issue: The text says the address type is bound to a 'port', while it is declared in the port type.

requirements.subject: ent:address-type
requirements.canonical: A value of the address type bound to a port MAY be used for addressing purposes in communication operations.
requirements.original: Values of this type may be used for addressing purposes in communication operations (see clause 22.1) and be stored in variables.

requirements.subject: ent:address-type
requirements.canonical: A value of the address type bound to a port MAY be stored in a variable.
requirements.original: Values of this type may be used for addressing purposes in communication operations (see clause 22.1) and be stored in variables.

requirements.subject: ent:message-based-port
requirements.canonical: A message-based port type definition has the syntax `type port` PortTypeIdentifier `message` "{" followed by any sequence of `address` Type ";", `map param` "(" FormalValuePar list ")", `unmap param` "(" FormalValuePar list ")" and (`in` | `out` | `inout`) MessageType list ";" entries, and "}".
requirements.original:
type port PortTypeIdentifier message "{"
     { (address Type ";") |
      (map param "(" { FormalValuePar [","] }+ ")") |
      (unmap param "(" { FormalValuePar [","] }+ ")") |
      ((in | out | inout) { MessageType [ "," ] }+ ";") } 
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:procedure-based-port
requirements.canonical: A procedure-based port type definition has the syntax `type port` PortTypeIdentifier `procedure` "{" followed by any sequence of `address` Type ";", `map param` "(" FormalValuePar list ")", `unmap param` "(" FormalValuePar list ")" and (`in` | `out` | `inout`) Signature list ";" entries, and "}".
requirements.original:
type port PortTypeIdentifier procedure "{"
     { (address Type ";" ) |
      (map param "(" { FormalValuePar [","] }+ ")") |
      (unmap param "(" { FormalValuePar [","] }+ ")") |
      ((in | out | inout) { Signature [ "," ] }+ ";") } 
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A constant, variable or formal parameter MAY be of a port type.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows to define constants, variables and parameters of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type-value
requirements.canonical: A constant, variable or formal parameter of a port type CAN contain a reference to an existing component port or the special value `null`.
requirements.original: These constants, variables or parameters can contain a reference to an existing component port or a special value null.

requirements.subject: ent:null-value
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` of a port type IS representing an unspecified port reference, i.e. the reference to no port.
requirements.original: The special value null represents an unspecified port reference, i.e. it can be used to explicitly allow the referencing of no port.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type-value
requirements.canonical: A port type value IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.
requirements.original: Port type values are object references and follow specific rules for this kind of values.

ambiguity.issue: 'specific rules for this kind of values' is not referenced to a clause.
readings: A port type value IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references defined in this standard.
A port type value IS an object reference; the rules applying to it are not specified in this clause.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type SHALL have at most one address type bound to it.
requirements.original: a) At most one address type shall be bound to a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type SHALL have at most one map parameter list defined.
requirements.original: b) At most one map parameter list shall be defined for a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type SHALL have at most one unmap parameter list defined.
requirements.original: c) At most one unmap parameter list shall be defined for a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter of a `map param` or `unmap param` declaration SHALL be a value parameter of a data type.
requirements.original: d) Formal parameters of map param and unmap param declarations shall be value parameters of a data type.

requirements.subject: ent:message-type
requirements.canonical: A MessageType in a message-based port type definition SHALL be a reference to a data type.
requirements.original: e) `MessageType shall be a reference to a data type.`

requirements.subject: ent:message
requirements.canonical: The term message IS used to mean both messages defined by templates and actual values resulting from expressions.
requirements.original: NOTE: The term message is used to mean both messages as defined by templates and actual values resulting from expressions.

requirements.subject: ent:message-based-port
requirements.canonical: The list restricting what may be used on a message-based port IS a list of type names.
requirements.original: Thus, the list restricting what may be used on a message-based port is simply a list of type names.
